subject: piti is not your expenses
preheader: the 50 percent rule is a rough screen, not a property fact.
headline: PITI and operating expenses answer different questions.
body: PITI means principal, interest, taxes, and insurance. Subtracting only those four items from rent can omit vacancy and other operating costs, so it is not a complete property-level cash-flow model.

Applicable lines may include management, vacancy, repairs, maintenance, capital reserves, lawn or snow service, owner-paid utilities, turnover, pest service, HOA dues, and other property-specific costs.

The 50% rule is an educational shortcut that assumes operating expenses before debt service equal half of gross rent. On $2,000 monthly rent, that shortcut leaves $1,000 before debt service. It does not establish the property's actual expenses or cash flow.

Property age, condition, tax, insurance, utilities, management scope, vacancy, and service obligations can all make the shortcut inaccurate. Use it only as a rough comparison, then replace it with reviewed line items.

TrueCap line-items every expense category and keeps tax and insurance visible. Enter the local property-tax bill and replace preliminary insurance assumptions with a current quote before relying on the operating-expense result.
